planting.note: Wait until soil has warmed well past the last frost date, since shrunken-2 kernels have almost no seed reserves and rot readily in cold, wet ground. Isolate from standard (SU) sweet corn or field corn by distance or planting date to prevent cross-pollination, which produces starchy, tough kernels.

directions: Direct sow into warm, fertile soil in blocks of at least four rows for dependable wind pollination. Illini Xtra Sweet was developed at the University of Illinois around the discovery and early commercialization of the shrunken-2 (sh2) gene, which keeps sugars from converting to starch after picking, giving it a longer sweet eating window than older sugary (SU) corns like Golden Bantam. Unlike most modern sh2 hybrids, it is open-pollinated, so seed can be saved from year to year as long as isolation from other corn types is maintained. Keep soil consistently moist from tasseling through ear fill, since the plant is somewhat less vigorous in cool or wet spring conditions than newer hybrid supersweets.
sources: University of Illinois Department of Crop Sciences — corn breeding history
Southern Exposure Seed Exchange catalog notes

planting.note: Start indoors 8 weeks before the last frost and transplant only once nights stay reliably above 55F. Classic is an upright, vigorous plant that benefits from staking as fruit load builds, and it holds fruit quality well through summer heat.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the soil has warmed, spacing plants far enough apart for good air circulation. Classic is a widely grown commercial hybrid bred for a heavy, uniform set of large, glossy black-purple, oval fruit on a productive, disease-tolerant plant, and it has become something of a benchmark against which other standard American-type eggplants are compared. Harvest fruit while the skin is still glossy and firm; dull, matte skin signals over-mature fruit with more seeds and a bitter edge. Consistent watering during fruit set is important, since moisture swings can trigger blossom drop and misshapen fruit.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — eggplant production

planting.note: Direct sow after soil has warmed and frost danger has passed; succession sow every two to three weeks for a continuous harvest of tender wax pods.

directions: Direct sow into well-drained soil in full sun once the ground has warmed. Improved Golden Wax is an early-twentieth-century refinement of the old Golden Wax bean, bred to add resistance to common bean mosaic and improve pod straightness while keeping the same flat, buttery-yellow, stringless pods and compact bush habit. Pick pods young, while still slender and snapping cleanly, since wax beans quickly develop tough strings and a fibrous texture if left to mature on the plant. Because it is an open-pollinated heirloom, seed can be saved for the next season by letting a few pods dry fully on the vine.

planting.note: Start indoors 6–8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into warm soil once nights stay above 55F. Galine's early maturity makes it a good option for gardeners in cooler, shorter-season climates who still want a classic elongated slicing eggplant.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after danger of frost has passed. Galine is a French-bred hybrid eggplant valued for its notably early maturity and reliable fruit set even in cooler summers, producing slender, cylindrical, glossy near-black fruit on a compact, manageable plant. The thin skin and few seeds make it well suited to quick-cooking preparations like grilling and stir-frying without the bitterness that can develop in larger, later-maturing types. Harvest at about two-thirds full size while the skin is taut and glossy for the mildest flavor and tenderest texture.

planting.note: Start indoors 8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into warm soil once nights stay reliably above 55F. Santana's tolerance of verticillium wilt makes it a dependable choice for gardens with a history of eggplant or tomato soil-borne disease.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the soil has warmed. Santana is a Dutch-bred hybrid eggplant selected for verticillium wilt tolerance and a heavy, extended set of glossy, deep-black, oval fruit on a vigorous, productive plant, making it a favorite of market growers who need consistent yields through a long season. The dense white flesh has few seeds and holds up well to roasting, grilling, and frying without becoming watery. Keep soil evenly moist and side-dress with compost or balanced fertilizer as fruiting begins to sustain production over the full harvest window.

planting.note: Direct sow after soil has warmed, in blocks of at least four short rows for reliable pollination. Trinity's cool-soil vigor and early maturity make it a good choice for a first succession planting in short-season gardens.

directions: Direct sow into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once the ground has warmed. Trinity is a synergistic (SY) bicolor hybrid that combines sugary-enhanced and supersweet genetics on the same ear, giving tender, creamy kernels with good sweetness retention without the tough pericarp of straight sh2 types. It is among the earliest-maturing bicolor hybrids available, germinating well in cooler soil than most supersweet corn and making it a reliable choice for gardeners wanting the first fresh corn of the season. Water consistently from tasseling through ear fill to ensure full, well-formed ears.
sources: Johnny's Selected Seeds variety trial notes
